items.name: Only legislative powers granted by the Constitution vest in Congress; the clau
items.summary: Only legislative powers granted by the Constitution vest in Congress; the clause does not confer a general federal police power.

items.name: The House is chosen every second year by the people of the states.
items.summary: The House is chosen every second year by the people of the states.

items.name: House electors in each state require qualifications for electors of the most n
items.summary: House electors in each state require qualifications for electors of the most numerous branch of that state's legislature.

items.name: A Representative must be at least 25, a U.S. citizen for seven years, and an i
items.summary: A Representative must be at least 25, a U.S. citizen for seven years, and an inhabitant of the electing state at election.

items.name: Actual enumeration is required within every subsequent term of ten years; init
items.summary: Actual enumeration is required within every subsequent term of ten years; initial three-year instruction was historically satisfied.

items.name: Each state is entitled to at least one Representative, with other House apport
items.summary: Each state is entitled to at least one Representative, with other House apportionment rules subject to later amendments.

items.name: The original text limits the number of Representatives to no more than one for
items.summary: The original text limits the number of Representatives to no more than one for every thirty thousand persons.

items.name: The original three-fifths apportionment formula is no longer operative after c
items.summary: The original three-fifths apportionment formula is no longer operative after constitutional abolition of slavery and changes to apportionment.
items.note: This is an original-text historical provision, not a presently valid population formula.

items.name: Amendment XIV Section 2 modified the original apportionment method.
items.summary: Amendment XIV Section 2 modified the original apportionment method.

items.name: State executive authority issues writs of election to fill House vacancies.
items.summary: State executive authority issues writs of election to fill House vacancies.

items.name: The House, not the Senate, chooses its Speaker and other House officers.
items.summary: The House, not the Senate, chooses its Speaker and other House officers.

items.name: The House alone exercises the constitutional power of impeachment.
items.summary: The House alone exercises the constitutional power of impeachment.

items.name: Each state has two Senators, with one vote per Senator and six-year terms.
items.summary: Each state has two Senators, with one vote per Senator and six-year terms.

items.name: The Seventeenth Amendment replaces the original state-legislature selection of
items.summary: The Seventeenth Amendment replaces the original state-legislature selection of Senators with election by the people.

items.name: Senators are distributed into three classes, with approximately one third sele
items.summary: Senators are distributed into three classes, with approximately one third selected every second year.

items.name: The Seventeenth Amendment changes vacancy procedures, permitting state executi
items.summary: The Seventeenth Amendment changes vacancy procedures, permitting state executive temporary appointments only if the legislature provides for them.

items.name: A Senator must be at least thirty, a U.S. citizen for nine years, and an inhab
items.summary: A Senator must be at least thirty, a U.S. citizen for nine years, and an inhabitant of the represented state when elected.

items.name: The Vice President presides over the Senate but may vote only when Senators ar
items.summary: The Vice President presides over the Senate but may vote only when Senators are equally divided.

items.name: Senate chooses a president pro tempore for the Vice President's absence or exe
items.summary: Senate chooses a president pro tempore for the Vice President's absence or exercise of presidential office.

items.name: Senators sitting to try impeachment are under oath or affirmation.
items.summary: Senators sitting to try impeachment are under oath or affirmation.

items.name: The Chief Justice presides if the President is tried on impeachment.
items.summary: The Chief Justice presides if the President is tried on impeachment.

items.name: Conviction on impeachment requires concurrence of two thirds of Senators prese
items.summary: Conviction on impeachment requires concurrence of two thirds of Senators present.

items.name: Judgment in impeachment extends no further than removal and possible disqualif
items.summary: Judgment in impeachment extends no further than removal and possible disqualification from federal office.

items.name: Conviction on impeachment does not insulate the convicted person from later in
items.summary: Conviction on impeachment does not insulate the convicted person from later indictment, trial, judgment or punishment under law.

items.name: State legislatures prescribe times, places and manner of federal congressional
items.summary: State legislatures prescribe times, places and manner of federal congressional elections, subject to Article I and later amendments.

items.name: Congress may make or alter state election regulations by law, subject to the c
items.summary: Congress may make or alter state election regulations by law, subject to the clause's stated original exception.

items.name: The original exception concerning places of choosing Senators must be assessed
items.summary: The original exception concerning places of choosing Senators must be assessed with the Seventeenth Amendment's introduction of popular Senate elections.
items.note: The original textual exception is acknowledged, but this research model does not independently determine its modern operation after the Seventeenth Amendment.

items.name: Congress shall meet at least once annually.
items.summary: Congress shall meet at least once annually.

items.name: The Twentieth Amendment Section 2 replaces the original default congressional
items.summary: The Twentieth Amendment Section 2 replaces the original default congressional meeting date.

items.name: Each House judges the elections, returns and qualifications of its own Members
items.summary: Each House judges the elections, returns and qualifications of its own Members.

items.name: A majority of the respective House constitutes a quorum to conduct business.
items.summary: A majority of the respective House constitutes a quorum to conduct business.

items.name: A smaller number may adjourn day to day and may compel attendance under the Ho
items.summary: A smaller number may adjourn day to day and may compel attendance under the House's prescribed procedures and penalties.

items.name: Each House makes its own rules and may punish its members for disorderly behav
items.summary: Each House makes its own rules and may punish its members for disorderly behavior.

items.name: Expulsion of a member requires the concurrence of two thirds.
items.summary: Expulsion of a member requires the concurrence of two thirds.

items.name: Each House must keep a journal and publish it from time to time.
items.summary: Each House must keep a journal and publish it from time to time.

items.name: Each House may withhold journal portions its judgment requires to remain secre
items.summary: Each House may withhold journal portions its judgment requires to remain secret.

items.name: On request of one fifth of Members present, yeas and nays on a question must b
items.summary: On request of one fifth of Members present, yeas and nays on a question must be entered on the journal.

items.name: During congressional session, adjournment for more than three days or relocati
items.summary: During congressional session, adjournment for more than three days or relocation to another meeting place requires the other House's consent.

items.name: Compensation for Members is ascertained by law and paid out of the United Stat
items.summary: Compensation for Members is ascertained by law and paid out of the United States Treasury.

items.name: Arrest privilege during covered attendance and travel excepts treason, felony
items.summary: Arrest privilege during covered attendance and travel excepts treason, felony and breach of the peace.

items.name: Speech or debate in either House cannot be grounds to question Members in any
items.summary: Speech or debate in either House cannot be grounds to question Members in any other place; doctrinal scope requires case-law analysis.

items.name: The Twenty-Seventh Amendment restricts when laws varying congressional compens
items.summary: The Twenty-Seventh Amendment restricts when laws varying congressional compensation take effect.

items.name: During their elected term, Senators and Representatives cannot be appointed to
items.summary: During their elected term, Senators and Representatives cannot be appointed to civil offices newly created or whose emoluments increased during that term.

items.name: A person holding an office under the United States cannot simultaneously be a
items.summary: A person holding an office under the United States cannot simultaneously be a Member of either House.

items.name: A bill raising revenue must originate in the House of Representatives.
items.summary: A bill raising revenue must originate in the House of Representatives.

items.name: The Senate may propose or concur with amendments to a House-originated revenue
items.summary: The Senate may propose or concur with amendments to a House-originated revenue bill.

items.name: Legislative bills must pass both Houses before Presidential presentment.
items.summary: Legislative bills must pass both Houses before Presidential presentment.

items.name: Passed bills are presented to the President for approval or returned objection
items.summary: Passed bills are presented to the President for approval or returned objections.

items.name: A presidential veto is overridden only if each House approves reconsideration
items.summary: A presidential veto is overridden only if each House approves reconsideration by two-thirds vote under the stated procedure.

items.name: For a veto override, each House must record yea/nay votes and Member names in
items.summary: For a veto override, each House must record yea/nay votes and Member names in its journal.

items.name: A bill not returned within ten days excluding Sundays generally becomes law ab
items.summary: A bill not returned within ten days excluding Sundays generally becomes law absent the constitutional adjournment exception.

items.name: If Congress adjourns in a way that prevents return of a bill, the no-return pa
items.summary: If Congress adjourns in a way that prevents return of a bill, the no-return passage rule does not apply.

items.name: Covered orders, resolutions and votes requiring bicameral concurrence are pres
items.summary: Covered orders, resolutions and votes requiring bicameral concurrence are presented for presidential approval or constitutionally prescribed repassage.

items.name: Questions of adjournment are expressly excepted from order/resolution/vote pre
items.summary: Questions of adjournment are expressly excepted from order/resolution/vote presentment.

items.name: Taxing and spending authority is directed to debts, common defense and general
items.summary: Taxing and spending authority is directed to debts, common defense and general welfare of the United States.

items.name: Duties, imposts and excises must be uniform throughout the United States.
items.summary: Duties, imposts and excises must be uniform throughout the United States.

items.name: Article I Section 9 Clause 4 requires apportionment for covered direct taxes s
items.summary: Article I Section 9 Clause 4 requires apportionment for covered direct taxes subject to the Sixteenth Amendment income-tax rule.
items.note: Model cross-text limits together; not an absolute ban on unapportioned income taxes.

items.name: Article I Section 9 Clause 5 separately forbids federal export duties.
items.summary: Article I Section 9 Clause 5 separately forbids federal export duties.
items.note: Source provision: Article I §9 cl5; links do not constitute additional independent grant.

items.name: Borrowing is permitted on the credit of the United States.
items.summary: Borrowing is permitted on the credit of the United States.

items.name: The textual commerce categories are foreign nations, among the several states,
items.summary: The textual commerce categories are foreign nations, among the several states, and Indian tribes; later doctrine is separately reviewable.

items.name: Naturalization rule must be uniform.
items.summary: Naturalization rule must be uniform.

items.name: Federal laws on the subject of bankruptcies must be uniform throughout the Uni
items.summary: Federal laws on the subject of bankruptcies must be uniform throughout the United States.

items.name: The listed power concerns coining money, domestic and foreign coin value, and
items.summary: The listed power concerns coining money, domestic and foreign coin value, and standards of weights and measures.

items.name: Counterfeiting power identifies securities and current coin of the United Stat
items.summary: Counterfeiting power identifies securities and current coin of the United States.

items.name: Congress may establish post offices and post roads, without this clause alone
items.summary: Congress may establish post offices and post roads, without this clause alone specifying a modern organizational model.

items.name: Exclusive rights to authors and inventors must be granted for limited times.
items.summary: Exclusive rights to authors and inventors must be granted for limited times.

items.name: Exclusive rights under the clause are directed to promoting progress of scienc
items.summary: Exclusive rights under the clause are directed to promoting progress of science and useful arts.

items.name: Exclusive rights attach to authors and inventors for their respective writings
items.summary: Exclusive rights attach to authors and inventors for their respective writings and discoveries.

items.name: Congress may constitute tribunals inferior to the Supreme Court; Article III d
items.summary: Congress may constitute tribunals inferior to the Supreme Court; Article III defines a distinct judicial vesting structure.

items.name: Punishment and definition are limited to piracies and felonies on the high sea
items.summary: Punishment and definition are limited to piracies and felonies on the high seas and offenses against the law of nations.

items.name: Congress may declare war, grant letters of marque and reprisal, and regulate c
items.summary: Congress may declare war, grant letters of marque and reprisal, and regulate captures on land and water.

items.name: No appropriation to raise and support armies may be for a term longer than two
items.summary: No appropriation to raise and support armies may be for a term longer than two years.

items.name: Congress may provide and maintain a navy; the adjacent Army two-year language
items.summary: Congress may provide and maintain a navy; the adjacent Army two-year language is not copied into this clause.

items.name: The textual rules power concerns government and regulation of land and naval f
items.summary: The textual rules power concerns government and regulation of land and naval forces.

items.name: Calling forth militia is for executing the laws of the Union, suppressing insu
items.summary: Calling forth militia is for executing the laws of the Union, suppressing insurrections or repelling invasions.

items.name: States respectively reserve the appointment of militia officers.
items.summary: States respectively reserve the appointment of militia officers.

items.name: States retain militia training authority according to the discipline prescribe
items.summary: States retain militia training authority according to the discipline prescribed by Congress.

items.name: Federal seat of government district is not to exceed ten miles square.
items.summary: Federal seat of government district is not to exceed ten miles square.

items.name: Exclusive district legislation is conditioned on cession by particular states
items.summary: Exclusive district legislation is conditioned on cession by particular states and congressional acceptance.

items.name: Exclusive jurisdiction over described federal enclaves depends on purchase wit
items.summary: Exclusive jurisdiction over described federal enclaves depends on purchase with consent of the legislature of the state where the place lies.

items.name: Described enclave purposes include forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards and o
items.summary: Described enclave purposes include forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards and other needful buildings.

items.name: Necessary and Proper laws execute other constitutionally vested powers; this i
items.summary: Necessary and Proper laws execute other constitutionally vested powers; this is not a free-standing grant of unlimited regulatory authority.

items.name: The prohibition on congressional prohibition of specified migration/importatio
items.summary: The prohibition on congressional prohibition of specified migration/importation before 1808 expired by its stated date.
items.note: Do not reactivate forced-labor regimes, historical slave trade, or importation tax power.

items.name: Original clause allowed a tax or duty no greater than ten dollars per person o
items.summary: Original clause allowed a tax or duty no greater than ten dollars per person on covered importation; not operative authority today.

items.name: Habeas suspension exception requires rebellion or invasion and that public saf
items.summary: Habeas suspension exception requires rebellion or invasion and that public safety may require suspension.

items.name: Congress cannot pass bills of attainder or ex post facto laws.
items.summary: Congress cannot pass bills of attainder or ex post facto laws.

items.name: Capitation and other direct taxes generally require apportionment according to
items.summary: Capitation and other direct taxes generally require apportionment according to enumeration.

items.name: The Sixteenth Amendment permits federal taxes on incomes without the apportion
items.summary: The Sixteenth Amendment permits federal taxes on incomes without the apportionment required for other direct taxes.

items.name: Articles exported from any state may not bear federal tax or duty.
items.summary: Articles exported from any state may not bear federal tax or duty.

items.name: Federal commerce or revenue regulation cannot prefer one state's ports over an
items.summary: Federal commerce or revenue regulation cannot prefer one state's ports over another's.

items.name: Covered vessels bound to or from one state cannot be forced to enter, clear or
items.summary: Covered vessels bound to or from one state cannot be forced to enter, clear or pay duties in another state.

items.name: Treasury money may be drawn only pursuant to appropriations made by law.
items.summary: Treasury money may be drawn only pursuant to appropriations made by law.

items.name: Regular statements and accounts of all public money receipts and expenditures
items.summary: Regular statements and accounts of all public money receipts and expenditures must be published.

items.name: The United States may not grant titles of nobility.
items.summary: The United States may not grant titles of nobility.

items.name: A covered federal officeholder may accept specified foreign presents, emolumen
items.summary: A covered federal officeholder may accept specified foreign presents, emoluments, offices or titles only with congressional consent.

items.name: States cannot enter treaties, alliances or confederations, grant marque/repris
items.summary: States cannot enter treaties, alliances or confederations, grant marque/reprisal, coin money or emit bills of credit.

items.name: States cannot designate other than gold/silver coin legal tender or pass bills
items.summary: States cannot designate other than gold/silver coin legal tender or pass bills of attainder, ex post facto laws or contract-impairing laws.

items.name: States may not grant titles of nobility.
items.summary: States may not grant titles of nobility.

items.name: State imposts or duties on imports or exports require congressional consent un
items.summary: State imposts or duties on imports or exports require congressional consent unless the express inspection-law exception applies.

items.name: The clause excepts only charges absolutely necessary for executing state inspe
items.summary: The clause excepts only charges absolutely necessary for executing state inspection laws.

items.name: Net proceeds of relevant state import/export duties must be used for the Unite
items.summary: Net proceeds of relevant state import/export duties must be used for the United States Treasury; congressional revision and control applies.

items.name: State duties of tonnage, forces and warships in peace, and compacts with state
items.summary: State duties of tonnage, forces and warships in peace, and compacts with states or foreign powers, are subject to specified congressional consent.

items.name: States may engage in war without prior congressional consent if actually invad
items.summary: States may engage in war without prior congressional consent if actually invaded or in such imminent danger as will not admit delay.
